title: Start March With One Question Worth Tracking
teaser: A good month can be organized around a useful question instead of a crowded goal list.
full_text: Choose one question you want March to answer through experience or evidence. Write what you will pay attention to during the month.

title: Remove One Hidden Step From a Routine
teaser: Small hidden steps can make simple routines harder to repeat.
full_text: Walk through one routine you use often and identify a step that exists only because something is stored, named or arranged poorly. Remove that friction if you can.

title: Check Who Benefits From a Metric
teaser: A number can improve one outcome while quietly harming another.
full_text: Take one metric you use to judge performance. Ask what behavior it rewards and what important behavior it might ignore.

title: Use a Default for a Low-Stakes Choice
teaser: Not every repeated choice deserves fresh attention.
full_text: Pick one low-stakes decision you make often and set a sensible default. Reserve deliberate thinking for cases where the default no longer fits.

title: Name the Tradeoff in a Yes
teaser: Every yes uses time, money or attention that cannot be spent elsewhere.
full_text: Before accepting one optional commitment today, name what you would give up to make room for it. Decide with both sides visible.

title: Keep a Useful Source With the Claim
teaser: Facts travel more safely when their origin stays attached.
full_text: For one important note or statistic today, store the source and date beside the claim. Make future verification possible without reconstructing your search.

title: Ask for a Definition Before Debating
teaser: People can disagree for a long time while using the same word differently.
full_text: In one discussion today, identify a key term that may be ambiguous. Agree on what it means in this context before arguing about the conclusion.

title: Use a Smaller Batch to Learn Faster
teaser: Large batches can hide mistakes until they become expensive.
full_text: For one repeatable task, process a smaller sample first and inspect the result. Scale up only after the method looks reliable.

title: Review a Backup Before You Need It
teaser: A backup is useful only if it contains what you expect and can be restored.
full_text: Check one important backup today. Confirm its date, contents and restore path rather than assuming the file alone is enough.

title: Give a Difficult Task a Clear Entry Point
teaser: Unclear starting conditions can create more resistance than the task itself.
full_text: For one demanding task, decide exactly where you will begin: the file, question, tool or first observable action. Leave that entry point ready.

title: Separate a Preference From a Requirement
teaser: Treating preferences as requirements can make choices unnecessarily rigid.
full_text: Review one decision you are making and label each criterion as required or preferred. See whether new options appear when the distinction is honest.

title: Record One Small Win Without Inflating It
teaser: Evidence of progress can be useful without turning every step into a major victory.
full_text: Write down one concrete thing that moved forward today and why it mattered. Keep the description specific enough to learn from.

title: Check the Cost of Switching Tasks
teaser: A full calendar can hide how much time transitions consume.
full_text: Notice one period today with frequent task switching. Estimate the minutes lost to reopening context and decide whether two tasks can be grouped.

title: Invite Correction Early
teaser: Early correction is often cheaper than defending a nearly finished mistake.
full_text: Show a rough piece of work to someone relevant before polishing it. Ask specifically what assumption or direction looks wrong.

title: Run a Mid-Month Capacity Check
teaser: Halfway through the month is early enough to adjust without abandoning the plan.
full_text: Compare your remaining March commitments with the time actually available. Remove or move one item if the load no longer fits.

title: Make One Shared Expectation Observable
teaser: Vague expectations create different definitions of success.
full_text: For one shared task, replace words like soon, careful or complete with an observable result, date or acceptance condition.

title: Check a Price Against Frequency of Use
teaser: Value often depends on repeated use rather than the purchase moment.
full_text: For one item or service you are considering, estimate how often you will realistically use it. Compare cost per use with a simpler alternative.

title: Trace a Problem to Its Earliest Signal
teaser: The best intervention point may appear long before the visible failure.
full_text: Review one recurring problem and identify the first signal that something is going off course. Decide whether a check can happen there instead.

title: Finish a Conversation With Written Agreement
teaser: Memory can turn the same conversation into different commitments.
full_text: After one important discussion, send or save a short summary of the decision, owner and next date. Let others correct it while details are fresh.

title: Protect a Small Piece of Unscheduled Time
teaser: Unscheduled space can absorb delays and create room for thought.
full_text: Leave one short block intentionally unassigned today. Notice whether it becomes recovery, transition or useful thinking rather than wasted time.

title: Check Whether a Shortcut Preserves the Important Part
teaser: Faster is only useful when the outcome that matters survives.
full_text: Take one shortcut you use often and name what quality it must preserve. If that quality is lost, redesign the shortcut instead of celebrating speed.

title: State a Limit Before Resentment Builds
teaser: Early boundaries are often easier to communicate than late frustration.
full_text: Identify one commitment that is approaching your limit. State the available time, scope or frequency before the situation becomes harder to discuss.

title: Give an Idea a Cheap Failure Mode
teaser: Experiments are safer when failure does not require a large recovery.
full_text: For one new idea, design the smallest version that can teach you something useful. Cap the time or money you are willing to lose before starting.

title: Look for Repeated Manual Entry
teaser: Repeated copying is a common source of both wasted time and silent errors.
full_text: Notice one workflow where the same information is entered twice. Explore whether one trusted source can feed both uses without reducing control.

title: Add a Quality Check to a Volume Goal
teaser: More output can hide declining usefulness.
full_text: Take one quantity you track and pair it with a simple quality signal. Decide what would count as enough output without sacrificing the standard.

title: Use a Two-Minute Setup for Deep Work
teaser: Preparation should reduce friction, not become another form of avoidance.
full_text: Before one difficult task, spend no more than two minutes opening what you need and writing the immediate objective. Then begin the real work.

title: Ask What Need Is Under the Request
teaser: Understanding the need can reveal more than one acceptable solution.
full_text: When someone asks for something today, ask what outcome they are trying to achieve if the request is unclear. Solve for the need rather than the first proposed method.

title: Put Dependencies Before Dates
teaser: A calendar date cannot rescue work that depends on unfinished prerequisites.
full_text: List the prerequisites for one upcoming deliverable. Order them before assigning dates so the schedule reflects what must happen first.

title: Reproduce a Problem Before Fixing It
teaser: A fix is hard to trust when the original failure cannot be observed reliably.
full_text: For one technical or process problem, capture the conditions that reproduce it. Apply the change and test the same conditions again.

title: Prepare the Month-End Review Before the Last Day
teaser: Good review is easier when closing tasks are not competing for the same hour.
full_text: Finish one small administrative or tracking task today that would otherwise crowd tomorrow. Leave the last day for interpretation rather than cleanup.

title: End March With One Transferable Lesson
teaser: A useful review turns experience into a rule you can test again.
full_text: Choose the most useful lesson March gave you and express it as a behavior for April. Make the behavior specific enough to notice whether you follow it.
